newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends touch firmer in lethargic session.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends touch firmer in lethargic session.

text.p: London cocoa futures finished narrowly firmer on Wednesday after a session marked by lack of direction and dismissal of crop news.
Traders said some short covering bids creeping into New York had spurred London in the afternoon after a lethargic morning. But sterling's renewed strength in currency markets held it back again.
The day's modest turnover of 4,950 lots contained a large chunk of switches and crosses.
"It's mainly floor generated -- it's the boys on the floor," said one trader referring to a lack of outright trade and industry interest.

The benchmark March contract closed one stg firmer on the day at 880 stg a tonne, a level that has proved a difficult barrier. It traded in a narrow range of 883 and 876 stg. Second-month May also ended one up at 901.
The March/May switch, which some traders say should take centre-stage given the large open interest on March, was trading steadily at 20-21 stg.
The market's apathy stems from clashing views among players about the availability of cocoa over the next few months.
"The market seems to have paralysed itself with fears about one thing or the other," said the trader.
Arrivals in West Africa are consistently below last year -- although they are likely to pick up in January and February -- but traders suspect the crop may have a long tail as it did last year.
"Prices are very weak. You're not going to buy a market that looks as if it's going to fall out of bed," said one.

Another unknown is the fate of 300,000 tonnes of physical cocoa believed to be in the hands of one trader. Key industry players and some trade shorts are betting on an aggressive liquidation and a drop in prices, but others say the trader may hold the market to ransom.

Technically, March needs to overcome the threat of 890 and 900 stg to pave the way for further gains. Support seems well built at 865 but failure to hold this could suggest a test of the 17-month low of 847 stg on second-month continuation basis.
On fundamental news, Ghana cocoa buyers expected arrivals to pick up from January with output seen closer to 350,000 tonnes.
"There is a lot of cocoa in the field," said one.
